subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: Which credential persistence and propagation contracts should OpenClaw support, and how should this umbrella be split across dashboard auth, Codex/OpenAI migration, runtime upgrade safety, and session-liveness tracking?
rationale: The remaining work crosses dashboard token persistence, OAuth refresh material ownership, provider fallback routing, installer/runtime compatibility, and terminal session semantics; these are product and security boundary choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Keep this issue as the coordinating umbrella and make each active subproblem own its security/product contract and proof path.

options.title: Close After Canonical Links
options.body: Close this umbrella only after maintainers designate narrower open issues as the sole canonical tracking items for every remaining acceptance criterion.

options.title: Run As Reliability Program
options.body: Treat this as one maintainer-led reliability program spanning auth, installer, runtime, and context management rather than a ClawSweeper repair candidate.

recommendation.title: Split Into Narrow Canonicals
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the coordinating umbrella and make each active subproblem own its security/product contract and proof path.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has recent history across macOS Dashboard auth, OpenAI/Codex migration, Codex auth bridge, doctor docs, and final-turn runtime fixes, making it the best available routing owner for the split decision.
